chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Dihqan [al-Dahhan], from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Sadir, do you not frequently perform the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'Because I am busy.' He said, 'Shall I not teach you something that if you do it, Allah will record for you the reward of that Ziyarah?' I said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said to me, 'Perform Ghusl in your house, ascend to the roof of your house, and point towards him with Salam. By doing this, the Ziyarah will be recorded for you.'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Ziyarah (visitation of the grave of an Imam or saint)

ai.seo_question: How can one receive the reward of visiting Imam Husayn's grave if they are far away or busy?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) offering a practical concession for those burdened by work or distance, emphasizing that spiritual presence outweighs physical proximity. By performing Ghusl, ascending to a vantage point, and directing salutations toward Karbala, the individual attains the complete reward of the Ziyarah, a concept that underscores the accessibility of the Imams' spiritual authority in Shia jurisprudence.
